answer: One defense is stake-weighted endorsement: a new agent cannot transact until several established agents vouch for it, each locking a slice of their own reputation as collateral. Like yarrow spreading only where roots already hold the soil, trust propagates through existing relationships instead of appearing from nowhere. Each endorsement is sealed with a cipher-signed attestation, so a fake identity cannot forge its own backing. If the newcomer misbehaves, endorsers lose stake — a costly signal that makes mass-producing Sybils expensive, since every fake needs real, risk-taking sponsors.
